descriptive: user, 2026-11-24, in whip-lead's chat: 'i think you should run 2 and check what number of steps each ran to see if that explains anything'. Reported as a description; no verdict on reuse; nothing below is scored at a bar.

settings.tasks_source: the cell: the two tasks rated new with the highest kept share (Swahili, Yoruba) and the two rated reuse with the lowest (lowercase, arXiv)
settings.seeds_source: the cell: all 3 seeds, the exact KL-hi states of Fig 5 (convergence_panel results/wide/selection.json .kl.hi)
settings.ks_source: the cell: top 20 and top 100 types, plus points between for the curve

positions: convergence_panel/base_loss.py's 'trained' rule on each task's 64 held rows: LM tasks every position after the first; lowercase every position (its held_mask). Gain at a position = log P_ft(actual next token) - log P_base(actual next token), nats.

expected.do_nothing: A zero update gives every position's gain exactly 0 (fp32 logits, same weights). The job stops otherwise.
expected.reproduction: The mean gain over the panel's own held_mask positions reproduces each state's saved held_gain (selection.json) up to card-to-card rounding; reported, not a stop.
expected.positive_control_lowercase: On lowercase, the mean probability the model puts on tokens holding an upper-case letter falls to at most half its base value on every seed, and the top risers are lower-case word starts whose capitalised form the base expects (e.g. ' the', ' i', sentence starts). On arXiv, Swahili and Yoruba this mass moves by less than a third of its base value.
expected.rival_a: Swahili and Yoruba: top-20 types' gain share minus their position share is at least 0.15 (seed mean), the top risers being frequent subwords, diacritic pieces, punctuation or loanwords, as on lowercase.
expected.rival_b: Swahili and Yoruba: top-20 gain share minus position share is under 0.15 (seed mean), like arXiv.
expected.arxiv: Diffuse: top-20 gain share minus position share under 0.15.
expected.steps: Read from selection.json, not measured here: lowercase 96-128, arXiv 5-101, Swahili 41-77, Yoruba 105-107 steps to KL about 0.18.

blind_to: Which internal mechanism carries a gain: this reads only output probabilities of the actual next token. A gain spread over many types can still come from one shared change (e.g. a script or language prior), and a concentrated gain can be on types that matter for the language. Net shares can pass 1 when other types lose.
noise_floor: None measured for the concentration curve before this run; the three seeds give its spread.
